Cluster sampling

Source: R/design-cluster.R
design_cluster.Rd

Selects whole clusters at random and returns all of their rows. The row count follows from which clusters were picked, so there is no n; use design_multistage() when you need to control it.

Usage

design_cluster(clusters, n_clusters, balanced = FALSE, na_rm = FALSE)

Arguments

clusters

Column naming each row's cluster.

n_clusters

Number of clusters to select.

balanced

Take an equal number of rows from each selected cluster, equal to the smallest selected cluster's size. See "Balanced clusters".

na_rm

Drop rows whose cluster label is NA instead of raising an error. When FALSE, missing labels are never treated as a cluster of their own.

Value

A design object, for use with draw().

Balanced clusters

With balanced = TRUE, each of the a clusters selected out of A gives m rows by simple random sampling, m being the size of the smallest of them. A row of a cluster of N_i rows has inclusion probability (a / A) * E(m) / N_i, where E(m) is the average take over the selections that include its cluster. inclusion_prob() computes it exactly: given that cluster i is selected, the take is at least s rows when the other a - 1 clusters selected all hold s rows or more, which happens with probability choose(c_s - 1, a - 1) / choose(A - 1, a - 1), c_s being the number of clusters of s rows or more, and E(m) adds these up for s from 1 to N_i. On clusters of 2, 4, 6 and 8 rows with two selected, that gives 0.5, 0.417, 0.333 and 0.25.

draw(weights = TRUE) weights a balanced sample conditional on the clusters it selected instead: .prob is (a / A) * m / N_i for the m taken in this draw. The estimate of a total is then A / a times the sum of the selected clusters' estimated totals, which is unbiased whichever clusters were selected, and so over all of them. ht_total() and ht_mean() use the two-stage variance of design_multistage(), with the variance between the estimated cluster totals and within each cluster, and as_svydesign() hands the sample to survey in two stages. The smallest selected cluster is taken whole and adds no variance within it. When it holds one row, every cluster gives one, the variation within clusters cannot be measured, and the variance falls back to the delete-a-cluster jackknife. Joint probabilities have no closed form; joint_prob() estimates them with simulate = TRUE.

See also

draw()

Other designs: design_bootstrap(), design_certainty(), design_multistage(), design_reservoir(), design_simple(), design_spatial(), design_spread(), design_stratified(), design_systematic(), design_temporal(), design_weighted()

Examples

df <- data.frame(id = 1:100, site = rep(paste0("s", 1:10), each = 10))
unique(draw(df, design_cluster("site", n_clusters = 3), seed = 1)$site)
#> [1] "s4" "s7" "s9"

# Balanced: the take is the smallest selected cluster's size, so a row of
# a large cluster is less likely to be drawn
uneven <- data.frame(site = rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), c(2, 4, 6, 8)))
bal <- design_cluster("site", n_clusters = 2, balanced = TRUE)
round(tapply(inclusion_prob(uneven, bal), uneven$site, unique), 3)
#>     a     b     c     d 
#> 0.500 0.417 0.333 0.250
